article.title: Useful phrases for starting a meeting
article.description: Common professional openers: 'Shall we get started?', 'Let's dive right in.', 'Thanks everyone for making the time.', 'I'd like to run through today's agenda.' Register: professional but not overly formal — appropriate for most workplace meetings. Avoid overly casual openers like 'What's up guys' in a professional context.
article.content: Common professional openers: 'Shall we get started?', 'Let's dive right in.', 'Thanks everyone for making the time.', 'I'd like to run through today's agenda.' generated.caption:
Ever worried about how to start a meeting in English? 🤔 Don't reach for 'What's up guys'!

To sound professional and confident, try these common openers instead. They're perfect for most workplace meetings. For example: 'Shall we get started?'

Save this for your next meeting and follow @TheEnglishVault for daily tips! 💼
generated.script: Professional meeting start karte waqt 'What's up guys' nahi bol sakte na? Toh sahi tareeka kya hai? Bahut log confuse ho jaate hain ki meeting kaise shuru karein without sounding too casual or too formal. 'What's up guys' jaise phrases toh bilkul avoid karne hain! Toh use kya karein? Aap bol sakte ho, 'Shall we get started?' jiska matlab hai 'chalo shuru karte hain'. Ya phir, 'Let's dive right in' – matlab, 'chalo seedha kaam ki baat karte hain'. 'Thanks everyone for making the time' bhi ek accha option hai jab aap sabko welcome kar rahe ho. Yeh phrases professional hain but not overly formal. Toh next time meeting start karte waqt, you know what to say! Professional, polite aur confident. Ab samajh aaya? Save kar lo ye reel next meeting ke liye aur comment mein batao aapko aur kaunsi phrases seekhni hain!

slides.body: Starting a professional meeting effectively sets the right tone from the outset. Instead of overly casual greetings, use phrases like 'Shall we get started?', 'Let's dive right in,' or 'Thanks everyone for making the time.' You can also say, 'I'd like to run through today's agenda' to smoothly transition into the discussion. These openers are professional yet not overly formal, making them perfect for most workplace settings. Remember to avoid informal phrases like 'What's up guys' in a professional context.
